title: Wrestle-Up Philosophy
shortDefinition: Wrestle-up turns guard from a defensive position into a controlled race to come on top.
whyItMatters: In no-gi, standing up or collecting a leg forces passers to respect threats instead of only passing.
deepExplanation: Wrestle-up is not random scrambling. It needs head position, safe chin, underhook or wrist control, hips under shoulders, and branches if sprawled on.
beginnerView: Stand when the head is high and hands have control.
advancedView: Use wrestle-up to connect guard, wrestling, passing, and mat returns.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Wrestle-Up Philosophy during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Wrestle-Up Philosophy to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Wrestle-Up Philosophy is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Wrestle-Up Philosophy before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
